catalog_entry.label: NFL Scouting Combine athletic testing results
contract_types: Pro Football Draft Combine: Longest Broad Jump
Pro Football Draft Combine: Player with Fastest 40 Time
catalog_entry.target: Probability that the best Combine measurement in a drill (40-yard dash, broad jump) clears a threshold or belongs to a named prospect, per official Combine results.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Combine drill extremes are the maximum (broad jump) or minimum (40-yard dash) over the prospects who are invited AND choose to perform the drill in Indianapolis. The outcome is generated in three layers: the invite pool and its position mix fix how many genuine speed and explosiveness candidates exist, at any position; each prospect's opt-in decision (injury, agent strategy, deferral to pro day) thins that pool, often removing the favourite; each participant's best-of-attempts result is his trained athletic ceiling plus attempt noise measured by the Combine's timing protocol. A threshold beyond the all-time record or an argmax among near-equal sprinters is therefore a tail and participation problem, not a draft-board problem.

inputs.why: Position-agnostic count of invitees with a fast prior sets how many draws reach the tail of the fastest 40 and longest broad jump; secondary because it aggregates the per-prospect prior.
A named prospect only wins the 40 market if he runs at the Combine; opt-outs of fast prospects reshape the argmax.
College track times, verified sprint data and size give each participant's expected 40 time and jump before he tests.
Best of typically two 40 attempts and multiple jumps raises each participant's result above his mean by a variance-dependent amount.
Yearly best 40 and broad jump over a provisional electronic-timing window, and the record, anchor the order-statistic tail for the 148-inch strike.
Electronic timing, start trigger, indoor track and unofficial-to-official revision define the recorded number that settles.
Reports that a prospect will not run, is injured, or will only test at his pro day update the participation hazard.
Projected top picks skip drills more often; board rank is a covariate for opt-out, not a predictor of speed.
Strike of 148 inches, Combine-only scope and the missing tie clause for the fastest 40 come from the contract text.
Broadcast unofficial 40 times are later revised to official times, which can reorder the top two sprinters.
Recorded official Combine result and its timestamp are needed to audit each settled market.
Drills run by position group on fixed days, so the market state jumps when the fastest groups test before close.

interactions.hypothesis: The fastest-40 probability of every other runner rises sharply when the prospect with the best prior declines to run, so opt-out news is worth more for elite priors.
The expected yearly best grows roughly with the log of the number of speed-position participants, so a thin receiver and corner class lowers the extreme.
Best-of-attempts helps a high-variance prospect whose mean trails the leader and hurts a favourite, so variance changes argmax share with a sign set by distance to the leader.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNFLCOMBINE-BROAD26-148 (floor_strike 148, greater_or_equal) resolves YES if any participant records a broad jump of at least 148 inches at the 2026 Combine; a pro-day jump does not count by the wording. KXNFLCOMBINE40-PLAYER26-ZTHO resolves YES if the named prospect records the fastest 40-yard dash at the 2026 Combine. Neither sampled text names the source of truth, whether unofficial or official times are used, or how a tie for fastest 40 is paid.

rules_evidence.quote: If any of the draft combine participants record a broad jump of at least 148 inches at the 2026 Pro Football Draft Combine, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A threshold on the maximum broad jump across all Combine participants, inclusive at 148 inches, limited to the Combine event itself.

rules_evidence.quote: If Zavion Thomas records the fastest 40-yard dash time in the 2026 Pro Football Draft Combine, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: An argmax market over all Combine 40 runners: the named prospect must both run at the Combine and post the minimum time.

variants_and_edge_cases: The 148-inch strike is one inch beyond the long-standing Combine broad-jump record of 147 inches (Byron Jones, 2015), so YES requires a new record; the probability is set by tail extrapolation, not by typical yearly bests.
The fastest-40 text has no dead-heat clause; official 40 times are reported to hundredths and a tie at the top is plausible, so payout under a tie is unknown.
Scope is the Combine only: a prospect who skips the Combine 40 and runs faster at his pro day cannot be YES, and his absence raises others' chances.
The text does not say whether broadcast unofficial times or later official times settle; these can differ by a few hundredths and reorder close sprinters.
rules_secondary is empty for both sampled markets, so no settlement source, revision window or void rule for a cancelled drill is visible.

Series scope verified on the Kalshi events API (2026-11-08): KXNFLCOMBINE-VERT26, -BROAD26, -BENCH26 and -4026 exist with settlement sources ESPN and NFL Network; only the broad-jump market text is sampled and the vertical and bench market rules could not be retrieved (markets no longer returned), so their tie and revision handling is unknown.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; presumably the official NFL Scouting Combine results published by the league (NFL.com Combine results), which is unverified.

mechanism.summary: The settling number is an order statistic over a self-selected field. About 320 prospects are invited; the league chooses the pool, so the count of wide receivers, corners, running backs and safeties determines how many plausible 4.2-second sprinters and 11-foot-plus jumpers exist. Each prospect then decides whether to perform each drill: injured players, projected top picks and players whose camps prefer a familiar pro-day surface opt out, which removes field members non-randomly and often removes the favourite. Each participant's result is his trained ceiling (from track background, college speed data and body mass) plus attempt-to-attempt noise, and the best of his attempts is recorded by the electronic timing system and later confirmed as official. The broad-jump strike sits above the all-time Combine record, so it is a record-break tail event; the fastest-40 contract is an argmax among a handful of near-equal sprinters where hundredths, ties and unofficial-versus-official revisions decide. Draft value, team needs and game statistics play no role in generating the measurement.

stages.name: Invite pool and positional composition
stages.description: The league's invite list (about 320-330 prospects, released in late winter) fixes the candidate field. Fastest 40 times come mostly from receivers, corners, safeties and running backs, while 11-foot jumps also come from edge rushers, linebackers and tight ends, so the pool is judged by pre-Combine prior rather than listed position: the number and quality of fast-prior invitees, and of small-school burners who were or were not invited, determine the size of the speed tail before anyone tests.
stages.distribution: Fixed count per class with year-to-year variation in speed-position share of roughly plus or minus 15 percent

stages.name: Drill opt-in decision by each invitee
stages.description: An invitee may skip the 40 or jumps because of injury, because his agent judges the risk of a slow time outweighs the upside, or because he prefers his pro day. Opt-out is concentrated among projected first-round picks and injured players and is announced through reports in the days before testing, so the realised field is a non-random thinning of the invite pool that can remove the best prior.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per prospect-drill with strong dependence on draft rank and injury; correlated within agencies

stages.name: Individual testing performance
stages.description: For each participant the recorded result is the best of his attempts, drawn around a personal ceiling set by sprint mechanics, track history and mass. Pre-Combine signals (college track 60 m or 100 m times, verified sprint data, prior hand times) predict the ceiling with error, and attempt noise plus a best-of-k rule shifts results toward the favourable tail for high-variance athletes.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal around the ceiling; sd of roughly 0.04-0.05 s per 40 attempt and 2-3 inches per jump are unsourced working estimates pending the random-effects fit; min of k draws

stages.name: Field extreme and argmax formation
stages.description: The broad-jump contract takes the maximum over all jumpers and asks whether it reaches 148 inches, one inch beyond the record; the 40 contract asks whether a named runner holds the minimum. Both depend on the extreme-value tail of the class, so the yearly-best history and its era trend calibrate the tail, and the argmax share of a favourite is bounded by the number of runners within a few hundredths of him.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value (Gumbel/Weibull-type) yearly best; record exceedance probability small and highly sensitive to tail shape

stages.name: Measurement, official revision and settlement
stages.description: The electronic timing protocol and indoor venue produce the recorded value; broadcast times shown as unofficial are later replaced by official times that can differ by a few hundredths. The contract text names no source, no revision window and no tie rule, so settlement mechanics are partly unknown and the recorded official number must be captured with timestamps.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official record; revision risk of a few hundredths that matters only when the top two are within 0.02 s

stages.name: Vertical-jump and bench-press events of the same series
stages.description: The Kalshi event list for KXNFLCOMBINE in 2026 has four events: highest vertical jump, longest broad jump, most bench-press reps and fastest 40. The vertical draws on the same elastic-power athletes as the broad jump, so it reuses their participation decisions with a correlated but distinct per-prospect prior. The bench press is a separate pool of interior linemen and edge players lifting 225 lb for reps, where heavier players with short arms do best and the main uncertainty is which strong prospects opt out. Both are field maxima settled on the official recorded result.
stages.distribution: Vertical: continuous half-inch maximum over roughly 150-250 jumpers, Gumbel-like tail; bench: integer maximum over roughly 150-200 lifters, upper tail driven by a few linemen, dead-heat ties possible

talent_strength.note: Prospect speed and lower-body power ceiling from pre-Combine evidence is the talent variable.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent: each prospect tests alone against the clock or tape; competition with the rest of the field is captured by the order-statistic tail and pool composition, not by a matchup.

role_personnel.note: Which positions and how many speed-position prospects are in the pool.

availability_news.note: Injury and opt-out reporting decides who actually runs and jumps.

coaching_scheme.note: Pre-draft training programmes (specialised speed camps) can improve 40 times by several hundredths between the college season and the Combine; no measured input captures which facility a prospect trained at or its effect.

environment.note: Indoor stadium track surface and timing setup are the environment; weather is irrelevant indoors.

game_context_script.note: No game is played: there is no score, clock or game flow, and drill order by position group does not change the measured values in any known way.

pace_volume.note: Number of participating prospects and attempts per prospect is the opportunity count.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of trained ceiling into the recorded best attempt.

distribution_variance.note: Extreme-value tail of the yearly best and attempt variance.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Draft-stock incentives drive the decision to test or defer to pro day.

officiating_rules.note: Timing method, attempt rules and unofficial-to-official revisions.

settlement_contract.note: 148-inch inclusive strike, Combine-only scope, missing tie and source clauses. Coverage is conditional on the two sampled markets; other drills in KXNFLCOMBINE are unresolved (u6).

nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.label: Combine invite pool size and position mix (aggregate of per-prospect priors, used as a covariate)
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.mechanism: The invite list fixes the field over which the fastest 40 and longest jump are taken. Candidates for the extreme come from any position with a fast prior (WR, CB, S, RB, and also edge, LB, TE for the jump), so the pool is filtered by prior, not by listed position.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.rationale: Yearly extremes vary with class composition: a class heavy in undersized receivers and corners produces more sub-4.35 runs and 11-foot jumps. Non-invited small-school prospects cannot settle the contract even if faster, so the invite list, not the draft class, defines the field.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.measurement: From the official invite list as of release date: counts by listed position, and for each drill the number of invitees whose nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior is faster than 4.40 s (40) or longer than 130 inches (broad), regardless of position. Derived aggregate of the per-prospect prior: in the per-prospect simulation it adds no information, and it is used only as the log(participants) covariate of the historical GEV fit in nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history. Compare to 2006-2025 classes as z-scores. As-of: invite release, refreshed with late additions.
free_sources: NFL.com official Combine invite list release
nflverse combine data (load_combine, sourced from Pro-Football-Reference)
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.why: Position-agnostic count of invitees with a fast prior sets how many draws reach the tail of the fastest 40 and longest broad jump; secondary because it aggregates the per-prospect prior.

nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.label: Combine drill opt-in probability per invitee and drill
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.mechanism: Each invitee independently decides whether to perform each drill in Indianapolis; skipping is driven by injury, draft-stock risk and preference for a pro-day surface.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.rationale: Opt-out is non-random: projected top picks and injured players skip more, and the fastest players sometimes run anyway to set records. Because the 40 contract is an argmax, a single opt-out of the best prior moves several percent of probability to each remaining contender.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.measurement: Logistic model of P(performed drill | invited) by drill, fit on 2010-2025 Combine data (missing value with player present = skip): covariates projected draft round from consensus board at invite date, injury reported in prior 60 days (yes/no), position, prior 40 tier; shrink team-agency effects with 20 prospects of prior weight. Update to 0 or 1 on credible reports in the final week; as-of each report timestamp.
raw_data: combine drill null flags by player
archived consensus board rank at invite date
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.why: A named prospect only wins the 40 market if he runs at the Combine; opt-outs of fast prospects reshape the argmax.

nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.label: Pre-Combine athletic prior (expected 40 time and broad jump per prospect)
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.mechanism: Each prospect's expected best Combine 40 and broad jump predicted from sprint and jump history, body mass and height before he tests.
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.rationale: College track results (60 m, 100 m, long jump), verified in-season GPS top speed when reported, and mass predict Combine times with an error of a few hundredths; heavier players with the same top speed run slower 40s because of acceleration. A prior is needed because the argmax is decided among a handful of prospects with similar reputations.
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.measurement: Regression of official Combine 40 (seconds) and broad jump (inches) on: best collegiate 60 m and 100 m (FAT, wind-legal), long jump, reported GPS max mph (flag source), weight and height, position; train on 2010-2025 participants with both measures; missing-track prospects get a position-weight prior; shrinkage toward position-weight mean with weight equal to 3 track races. Output mean and sd per prospect; as-of day before testing.
raw_data: reported GPS top speed with source and date
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.why: College track times, verified sprint data and size give each participant's expected 40 time and jump before he tests.

nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.label: Within-prospect attempt noise and best-of-attempts uplift
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.mechanism: The recorded value is the best of a prospect's attempts, so the expected recorded extreme exceeds his mean by an amount that rises with attempt variance and attempt count.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.rationale: Attempt-to-attempt 40 variation (start reaction, stumbles, hamstring tightness) is roughly a few hundredths (unsourced estimate until fitted); best-of-two shifts the expected best by roughly 0.56 sd. For a record-break threshold or a close argmax, this variance matters as much as the mean.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.measurement: From seasons where both 40 attempts and all jump attempts are published, estimate within-prospect sd by drill and position via random-effects model; where only best marks exist, infer sd from the gap between Combine and pro-day results for prospects who ran both (sd_attempt = sd_gap / sqrt(2) after removing a mean surface effect). Output sd and expected best-of-k uplift; units seconds and inches.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference pro-day and combine pages (free, scrape)
raw_data: combine attempt-level forty_1, forty_2 when published
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.why: Best of typically two 40 attempts and multiple jumps raises each participant's result above his mean by a variance-dependent amount.

nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.label: Yearly Combine best marks by drill (40, broad jump, vertical, bench reps) and record tail
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.mechanism: Distribution of the yearly fastest 40, longest broad jump, highest vertical and most bench-press reps across classes, used to calibrate the extreme-value tail of each drill and the chance of breaking its record.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.rationale: The 148-inch strike exceeds the 147-inch record, so the per-class probability is a record-exceedance tail that cannot be read from typical yearly bests; the era trend (training specialisation) and the number of participants shift the location.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.measurement: From nflverse Combine data 2006-2025 (fixed window; earlier timing regime excluded), take each year's best 40 time (minimum), broad jump (maximum, inches), vertical (maximum, inches) and bench press (maximum reps at 225 lb) among participants. For the three continuous drills fit a GEV to the 20 yearly maxima (sign-flipped for the 40) with location mu = a + b x (season-2006) + c x ln(number of participants who recorded the drill); shape by maximum likelihood with a Normal(0, 0.15) prior. For bench reps (integer) fit the same GEV to yearly maxima and discretise by rounding with continuity correction. Parametric bootstrap 2,000 draws for intervals. Output P(max >= x) for any strike and the distribution of the winning mark per drill. As-of before testing, using the forecast participant count per drill.
raw_data: combine.season, player, pos, forty, broad_jump, vertical, bench
participant counts by drill, position and year
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.why: Yearly best 40 and broad jump over a provisional electronic-timing window, and the record, anchor the order-statistic tail for the 148-inch strike.

nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.label: Combine timing protocol, track surface and unofficial-to-official revision
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.mechanism: How the recorded number is produced: electronic start and finish timing, indoor track surface, attempt rules, and the revision of broadcast unofficial times to official times.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.rationale: Unofficial broadcast times and official results can differ by a few hundredths, and timing-system changes across years shift the whole distribution; both matter for an argmax among sprinters separated by 0.01-0.03 s and for comparing a record across eras.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.measurement: For each Combine since 2015: document timing system and start method from league releases; compute mean and sd of (official minus first-displayed unofficial) 40 times from captured broadcast or tracker snapshots; flag years with a declared timing or surface change as regime breaks; output revision distribution in seconds and a regime indicator.
free_sources: league press releases on Combine format
raw_data: tracker snapshot player, drill, value, official flag, timestamp
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.why: Electronic timing, start trigger, indoor track and unofficial-to-official revision define the recorded number that settles.

nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.label: Bench-press (225 lb reps) participant pool and per-prospect rep prior
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.mechanism: The most-reps event is a maximum over prospects who choose to bench, a pool dominated by defensive and offensive linemen with long-standing strength histories; arm length lowers reps, and top prospects and players with upper-body injuries often skip the lift.
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.rationale: The speed and jump pools used for the 40 and broad jump are almost disjoint from the bench pool, so the existing priors say nothing about this event; the favourite is set by a few interior linemen with very high strength priors, and opt-outs among them change the maximum more than anything else.
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.measurement: Per invitee: expected reps = regression on 2006-2025 Combine bench results of position group (iDL, EDGE, OL, LB, TE, RB, other), weight (lb), arm length (in), and reported pro-day or college strength numbers where available (flagged by source), with prospect-level SD from residuals; shrink toward position-weight mean with weight 2 reported lifts. Participation probability from nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard refit for the bench drill (covariates: projected round, upper-body injury in prior 90 days, position). Simulate the field maximum over participating invitees (integer reps); calibrate the yearly maximum against the 2006-2025 history in nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history. Output P(max reps >= k) and P(named prospect has the most reps), dead-heat ties shown separately. As-of the day before bench testing.
free_sources: NFL.com Combine invite list and measurements (arm length)
raw_data: combine: season, player, pos, wt, bench (reps)
invite list measurements: arm length, weight
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.why: KXNFLCOMBINE-BENCH26 (Most Bench Press Reps) exists in the series; its pool and prior are lineman-driven and not covered by the speed/jump inputs.

nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.label: Vertical-jump participant pool and per-prospect jump prior
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.mechanism: The highest vertical is a maximum over jumpers whose ceiling depends on elastic power relative to mass; receivers, corners, safeties and some running backs and edge rushers populate the tail, and the event shares participants and opt-out behaviour with the broad jump.
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.rationale: Vertical and broad jump are correlated (both lower-body power) but not interchangeable: the vertical favours lighter, elastic athletes, measurement uses the Vertec standing-reach protocol, and best-of-attempt noise is larger relative to the spread of the top of the field, so the broad-jump prior cannot be reused unchanged.
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.measurement: Per invitee: expected vertical (inches) = regression on 2006-2025 Combine results of broad-jump prior from nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior, weight, height, position, and college track jump marks where available (long jump, high jump; FAT/wind-legal flags), with residual SD per position; participation from nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard refit for the vertical; joint simulation with the broad jump using the empirical residual correlation (estimated per position group, shrunk to pooled with weight n/(n+50)). Field maximum by simulation; output P(max >= x) for half-inch strikes and P(named prospect highest), ties reported. Calibrate yearly maxima to the 2006-2025 history. As-of the day before jumps.
raw_data: combine: season, player, pos, ht, wt, vertical, broad_jump
track jump marks with wind and timing flags
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.why: KXNFLCOMBINE-VERT26 (Highest Vertical Jump) exists in the series and needs its own prior and its correlation with the broad-jump field already modelled.

nfl.news.reason: Useful only as the channel for opt-out and injury reports in the final week; it does not inform speed, so it feeds the participation hazard rather than the outcome directly.

nfl.draft_board.reason: Consensus rank is a covariate for skipping drills (top picks opt out more) but carries almost no information about who is fastest; the blueprint's primary role for pick markets does not transfer here.

m.rules_text.reason: The inclusive 148-inch strike and the Combine-only scope come from the text, and the absence of tie and source clauses is itself a material contract risk.

m.stat_correction_risk.reason: Unofficial-to-official 40 revisions of a few hundredths can flip the fastest runner; for the broad jump the risk is smaller because jumps are taped in whole inches.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Needed to audit settled outcomes and to build the history, but not a predictive input; the source itself is not named in the rules.

m.lifecycle.reason: Position groups test on scheduled days, so whether the market closes before or after the receiver and corner groups run defines how much is known at close.

interactions.mechanism: The fastest-40 probability of a named runner depends on which other elite priors actually run; if the top prior opts out, the remaining contenders gain argmax share in proportion to their closeness to the new top, so the value of an opt-out report is larger the more dominant the absent prior was.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2010-2025 classes, compare realized fastest-40 share of the second-best prior in years where the top prior skipped versus ran.

interactions.mechanism: The expected yearly best improves roughly with the log of the number of speed-position participants: adding ten more corners shifts the best 40 by much less in a deep class than in a thin one, so the record-break probability is concave in pool size.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yearly best 40 and broad jump on log participant count in speed positions with a season trend; test curvature versus a linear count term.

interactions.mechanism: Under best-of-attempts the chance of the extreme mark depends on variance relative to the leader. For a runner whose mean is behind the target or the current leader, higher attempt variance raises his argmax or threshold chance; for the favourite, higher variance lowers it. The 148-inch tail effect is therefore signed by distance from the target, not uniformly convex.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized extremes against simulated ones using mean-only versus mean-plus-variance priors, splitting prospects into ahead-of and behind-the-leader by prior; check that the variance effect flips sign across that split.

interactions.mechanism: Revision of unofficial to official 40 times only matters when the two fastest official times are within the revision sd (about 0.01-0.02 s); outside that band revisions cannot change the argmax, so the settlement risk switches on only for close races.
interactions.how_to_test: From tracker snapshots, count classes where the leader changed between first-displayed and official times as a function of the gap between first and second.

interactions.mechanism: Vertical and broad jump outcomes are positively correlated within a prospect and opt-outs are usually joint (a prospect who skips jumps skips both), so the vertical and broad-jump maxima are dependent: one elite jumper opting out lowers both, and pricing the two events independently misstates their joint.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2006-2025 classes correlate yearly vertical and broad maxima and the identity of the leaders; test per-prospect joint skip rates for the two jumps.

nonlinearities.why: Probability of the yearly best broad jump reaching 148 inches falls faster than exponentially beyond the 147-inch record if the tail is bounded (negative GEV shape), so the estimate is dominated by the fitted shape parameter.

When a single dominant prior moves from likely to run to will not run, each remaining contender's fastest-40 probability jumps discretely rather than smoothly, because the argmax is over a small set of near-equal runners.
A runner's fastest-40 probability rises sharply as his expected time moves within a few hundredths of the best prior and is near zero beyond about 0.08 s, a logistic-like shape in the gap.

any player single-game rushing yards over 225 in season (other KXNFLGAMESPECIALS stats and quarter-specific markets unsampled)
catalog_entry.target: Probability that the maximum (or argmax) of a per-game quantity (game margin, game total, team points, player single-game rushing yards; other player stats unsampled) across a week's or season's slate of games exceeds a threshold or falls on a named game/team.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Each contract reads the extreme of one per-game quantity over a set of games: the season's largest final margin, largest total including overtime, any player's rushing yards in one game, or which game or team scores most in one week. The extreme is produced by the few games with the most lopsided talent pairings, quarterback absences, calm conditions for totals (dome or mild weather) and, for margins, any weather since bad conditions can widen mismatches and runaway scripts (turnover cascades, defensive touchdowns, a leader that keeps scoring). Probability is one minus the product of per-game non-exceedance over remaining games for season thresholds, with shared team-rating error adding dependence; for weekly argmax it is a simulation over the slate's integer score distributions with dead-heat splitting.

inputs.why: Season thresholds settle YES once any game clears the rung, so the realised maximum to date and remaining games define the live state.
Per-game probability that the final margin exceeds 51.5 points is a deep tail of the margin distribution conditioned on mismatch.
Per-game probability that combined points exceed 109.5 is a far upper tail of the game-total distribution.
Weekly argmax of game totals across the slate, with shared weather correlation and payout splitting.
Separate offence and defence scoring rates give each team's point distribution for the weekly highest-scoring team.
The 225+ rushing-yard contract needs per player-game exceedance probability combining carry volume and long-run tail.
A 52-point margin needs the leading team to keep scoring after the game is decided; coach and backup-QB behaviour set that.
Number of games and teams on the weekly slate (byes, Week 18 full slate) sets the baseline argmax share.
Integer scores tie at the weekly maximum often enough that the 1/N dead-heat payout changes expected value.
Historical season maxima of margin, total and single-game rushing yards by era anchor the tail and the rung choice.
Market-free team ratings give the pairing mismatches that generate blowouts and the expected scoring for shootouts.
A team's rating error is shared across its remaining games, which correlates per-game tail events for season maxima.
Backup or rookie quarterbacks on bad teams create the deepest mismatches that produce 50-point margins.
Very high totals need both teams to score; the joint upper tail of the two scores, not the sum of marginals, sets P(total > 109.5).
Benchmark only: P(OT) is binned by closing spread and total; the market-free overtime input is nfl.ot_model.
Wind, cold and rain suppress totals outdoors, so the weekly highest-scoring game leans toward domes and calm venues.
Defensive and return touchdowns add points without offence and accelerate runaway margins.
Benchmark only: team rush attempts are conditioned on the closing spread; carry volume uses nfl.carries with a market-free margin.
Per-carry explosive probability of the rusher decides whether volume turns into 225 yards.
Leading teams feed the back late, so blowout scripts add carries for the 225-yard contract.
Weak run defences allowing explosive runs are where single-game rushing records happen.
Starters are pulled at large margins, capping both further margin growth and a starter's single-game yardage.
Late-season resting of starters creates mismatches and lowers the scoring of resting teams in the weekly argmax.
The current kickoff regime shifts field position and scoring rates, so era base rates must be adjusted for it.
Regular-season scope, over-rung strikes, overtime inclusion and dead-heat 1/N splitting are read from the contract text.
Official rushing-yard corrections after a game can move a 223-227 yard performance across the 225 rung.
Weekly argmax markets are partly settled by earlier kickoff windows, so the running in-week maximum and close time condition the remaining games.
Integer team-score key-number PMF drives the weekly team and game argmax and the tie mass at the top; rates alone do not give it.
Weekly market close time relative to the last window (timing only, no price) sets how much of the week is already realised.
P(tie after regulation) from the market-free margin distribution and OT points under the current rule add the overtime mass that KXNFLHIGHSCORE explicitly counts.
Lead-back carry share and lead/trail-conditioned team rush attempts give the 28+ carry upper tail a 225-yard game needs.

interactions.hypothesis: Backup-QB and rested-starter shocks on the weak side are sub-additive in rating loss, so the deepest margins need a mismatch compounded by availability loss without double counting the tail convexity.
Once a lead passes about 35 points, further margin growth depends on whether the leader keeps calling scoring plays, so the margin tail is switched by coach policy.
225 rushing yards needs both 25+ carries from a leading script and at least two long runs, a product of volume and tail that is concentrated in blowout wins.
More teams near the top of the weekly score distribution raise both the competition for the argmax and the chance of a dead-heat split.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNFLBLOWOUT-27-52 resolves YES if any 2026-27 regular-season game ends with winner minus loser score over 51.5 points (score 'at the conclusion of the game'; overtime inclusion is inferred, not stated). KXNFLHIGHSCORE-27-110 resolves YES if any regular-season game, explicitly including overtime, has over 109.5 total points. KXNFLGAMESPECIALS-27-225RY resolves YES if any player records 225+ rushing yards in one regular-season game (overtime treatment of the full-game rung is silent). KXNFLWEEKGAMEHIGH and KXNFLWEEKHIGHSCORE resolve YES if the named game or team scores most in the stated week, ties paying $1/N rounded down to the cent (overtime not addressed). No sampled text names a stat source agency; cancelled or no-contest games are unaddressed.

rules_evidence.quote: Point differential is calculated by subtracting the losing team's score from the winning team's score at the conclusion of the game.
rules_evidence.establishes: Margin is the final score difference at game end; overtime points are inferred to count (the text does not say so) and a tie cannot qualify; only regular-season games are in scope.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a game (including overtime) with over 109.5 total points scored in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season maximum of game totals with overtime explicitly included; strike is strictly over the half-point rung.

rules_evidence.quote: If any player records 225+ rushing yards in any individual game during the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season maximum of single-game rushing yards over all players, inclusive at 225, regular season only.

rules_evidence.quote: any quarter-specific markets only pertain to stats recorded in an individual quarter, not inclusive of overtime.
rules_evidence.establishes: The series also carries quarter-specific variants whose window excludes overtime, which differ from the full-game rushing contract.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple games are tied for the most total points scored in Week 8,
rules_evidence.establishes: Weekly highest-scoring game uses a dead-heat split across tied games rather than voiding or awarding all.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Tennessee vs Cincinnati Pro Football game originally scheduled for Nov 1, 2026 is the highest scoring game in Week 8
rules_evidence.establishes: The game is identified by its original schedule date, so postponement handling depends on the week assignment, which the text does not spell out.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is the highest scoring team in Week 18 of the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Weekly argmax of team points across all teams playing that week, with a parallel 1/N tie rule.

rules_evidence.quote: any quarter-specific markets only pertain to stats recorded in an individual quarter, not inclusive of overtime
rules_evidence.establishes: The series carries quarter-window variants and excludes overtime from them, so a separate per-quarter chain is required.

variants_and_edge_cases: Season contracts (BLOWOUT, HIGHSCORE, GAMESPECIALS) settle YES as soon as one game clears the rung and otherwise NO after Week 18; the live price must use the realised maximum to date.

Only HIGHSCORE states overtime inclusion; BLOWOUT uses the score at the conclusion of the game, so OT inclusion is inferred there, and the weekly markets and the GAMESPECIALS full-game rung are silent on OT; a game tied after OT has margin zero.
Weekly argmax contracts pay $1/N rounded down to the nearest cent when tied, so No receives slightly more than (N-1)/N; integer scores and key numbers make ties non-trivial.
A team on bye in the named week cannot score, so its weekly market is effectively NO; Week 18 has every team playing while mid-season weeks have byes and fewer games.
KXNFLGAMESPECIALS includes quarter-specific markets that exclude overtime; only the 225+ rushing-yard full-game variant was sampled, so other stats and rungs in the series are unseen.

Rungs differ in rarity: 109.5 total is beyond the post-merger record (106, CIN 58-48 CLE 2004); a margin over 51.5 has occurred at least five times post-merger (LA Rams 59-0 ATL 1976, CIN 61-7 HOU 1989, NE 59-0 TEN 2009, NO 62-7 IND 2011, SEA 58-0 ARI 2012), roughly once a decade; 225+ rushing yards is a recurring event (record 296) rather than a record tail; base rates must be set per rung.

Cancelled or no-contest games (for example the 2022 BUF-CIN game) and postponed games are not addressed in the sampled text for season or weekly markets; treatment of their scores is unknown (see u5).

KXNFLGAMESPECIALS market list verified on the Kalshi events API (2026-11-08): passing yards 475/500/525, passing TDs 6+, rushing 225-300, receiving yards 250/275/300, receptions 15/17/20, 100 rush + 100 rec, non-passing TDs 4+, sacks 4/5/6, tackles 20+, defensive INTs 2/3 (settled YES), D/ST TDs 2+, and quarter rungs 250 passing / 150 rushing / 150 receiving.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; final scores and official player statistics as published by the league are the presumed source.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Only the 225+ rushing-yard full-game market was sampled; quarter-specific markets and other player stats (passing, receiving, touchdowns), if listed, are driven by player volume and quarter-window mechanics that this archetype's inputs do not cover.
series_mapping_issues.belongs_in: NEW_ARCHETYPE_NEEDED: player single-game stat specials (non-rushing and quarter-window rungs), conditional on such markets being listed

mechanism.summary: Each contract reads one extreme over many games, so the contributing games are a small, identifiable subset. Margins above 50 arise only when a strong team meets a weak one, usually with a backup quarterback, and the game script snowballs through turnovers, short fields and non-offensive touchdowns while the leader keeps scoring rather than kneeling. Totals above 109.5 require two good offences in a dome or calm weather, weak defences and often overtime, with positively correlated team scores. A 225-yard rushing game needs a lead back with 25-35 carries in a winning script plus two or more long runs against a weak run defence. The weekly highest-scoring game or team is an argmax over 13-16 games or 26-32 teams with heterogeneous integer score distributions, so the slate size, weather spread and tie mass matter as much as a single matchup. For season thresholds, P(YES) = 1 - product over remaining games of P(not exceed), modified by shared rating error, and the realised maximum to date resolves the market early.

stages.name: Pairing strength and quarterback state across the slate
stages.description: Talent gaps between paired teams set where extremes can occur. The season schedule fixes about 272 pairings; market-free team ratings with their posterior uncertainty, quarterback status (backup or rookie starters) and late-season resting of starters determine which few games carry most of the blowout and shootout probability.
stages.distribution: Heterogeneous per-game means; rating errors shared within team across games; mismatch counts heavily right-skewed

stages.name: Per-game score distribution and environment
stages.description: For every game, a pair of integer team-score distributions is generated from offence and defence scoring rates, pace and weather, with positive covariance through shared tempo and conditions and overtime adding points to tied games. This stage produces the weekly argmax inputs and the bulk from which the season tails are drawn.
stages.distribution: Discrete team-score PMFs with key-number atoms; game totals right-skewed; OT adds a small mass of extra points

stages.name: Runaway script and tail generation
stages.description: Extremes come from cascades: early turnovers giving short fields, pick-sixes and return touchdowns, and a trailing team forced to pass into a strong rush. Whether the margin keeps growing past 35-40 points depends on the leader's policy after pulling starters and on backup quarterbacks; weather lowers totals but not margins (the 59-0 game in 2009 was played in snow), and very high totals need both sides to keep scoring rather than one side collapsing.
stages.distribution: Heavy upper tails (generalized Pareto above about 21 points of margin); totals tail thicker than normal

stages.name: Player single-game rushing extreme
stages.description: For the 225-yard contract, the relevant subset is lead backs and running quarterbacks in winning scripts against weak run defences. Yards are carries times a per-carry distribution with a long right tail, so the event needs high volume plus two or more explosive runs; late-lead clock carries add volume, while a starter pulled in a blowout caps it.
stages.distribution: Compound: negative-binomial carries times heavy-tailed per-carry yards; season max over about 64 starting backs per week

stages.name: Aggregation to slate extremes and tie handling
stages.description: Weekly contracts take the argmax over the games or teams actually playing, so byes, slate size and the integer-score tie mass at the top determine baseline shares and dead-heat payouts. Season contracts multiply non-exceedance across remaining games, adjusted for shared rating error, and condition on the realised maximum to date, which can end the market early. Weekly argmax contracts are also conditioned on scores already realised in earlier kickoff windows before the market closes.
stages.distribution: Order statistic over 13-16 games or 26-32 teams; ties with probability of several percent at common totals; season P saturating in games remaining

stages.name: Settlement wording and record verification
stages.description: Contract text fixes regular-season scope, strict over-rung strikes for margin and total, inclusive 225 for rushing yards, overtime inclusion and the 1/N rounding-down dead-heat rule. No source agency is named, and official rushing-yard corrections after the game can move a near-rung performance across the line before settlement.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given final official data; residual correction risk near the rung

stages.name: Other player single-game specials: passing, receiving, TDs and defensive counts
stages.description: The live KXNFLGAMESPECIALS list for 2026-27 has rungs on passing yards (475/500/525), passing TDs (6+), receiving yards (250/275/300), receptions (15/17/20), non-passing TDs (4+), sacks (4/5/6), tackles (20+), defensive interceptions (2/3), D/ST TDs (2+) and 100 rushing plus 100 receiving yards, besides rushing. Each is a season-long any-player tail with its own process: passing and receiving rungs need shootout scripts and a concentrated target tree, sacks need a dominant rusher against a trailing team, tackles need heavy opponent run volume and generous scorers, and interceptions need a turnover-prone passer. Rungs already reached (2 and 3 interceptions, 15 and 17 receptions) are settled and drop out.
stages.distribution: Per player-game exceedance probabilities from overdispersed counts and heavy-tailed yardage; season event = 1 minus product over about 9,000 relevant player-games, sensitive to tail calibration

stages.name: Quarter-window specials with overtime excluded
stages.description: Three rungs ask for 250 passing, 150 rushing or 150 receiving yards inside one regulation quarter. The window makes possession count and explosive plays dominate: end-of-half two-minute drills and fourth-quarter comeback passing create the high-volume quarters, and one long touchdown can supply most of a 150-yard quarter. The rules text excludes overtime from quarter-specific markets, so the fifth period never counts.
stages.distribution: Per player-quarter heavy-tailed sum of a negative-binomial number of plays with long right-tail play yards; season event over roughly 36,000 relevant player-quarters

talent_strength.note: Team strength gaps and separate scoring rates generate mismatches and shootouts.

opponent_matchup.note: Pairing mismatch for margins and run-defence weakness for the rushing extreme.

availability_news.note: Quarterback injuries and late-season rest create the mismatches.

coaching_scheme.note: Run-it-up versus kneel behaviour and clock-killing carry policy.

environment.note: Dome and weather spread steer the weekly argmax and the season total tail.

game_context_script.note: Runaway scripts, starter pulls and overtime.

pace_volume.note: Number of games or teams in the slate and carry volume.

efficiency_conversion.note: Points per drive, per-carry tail and non-offensive scoring.

distribution_variance.note: Tail shapes, order statistics and tie mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Late-season rest and bye-driven slate size.

officiating_rules.note: Rule regime shifts scoring rates; crew penalty tendencies have no demonstrated effect on extremes.

settlement_contract.note: Strike construction, OT inclusion, 1/N dead heat and early YES settlement.

nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.label: Running season extreme to date and remaining eligible games
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.mechanism: For season-maximum contracts, the realised largest margin, total and single-game rushing yards so far, whether the rung is already cleared, and the list of remaining regular-season games define the live state.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.rationale: A season threshold is a first-passage event: once cleared it is YES, otherwise probability decays with each completed game. The relevant remaining exposure is not uniform: late-season weeks with rested starters and eliminated teams carry more blowout potential than mid-season weeks.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.measurement: After each completed game g update running maxima: M_margin = max |home-away|, M_total = max (home+away, OT included), M_rush = max player rushing yards (single game). For each rung r: cleared_r = 1[M >= r]. For remaining games compute p_g(r) from nfl.deep_tail_margin_model, nfl.total_distribution_tail and nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_rate respectively, using the shared team-rating draw (nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error) in 20,000 simulations rather than an analytic product. P(YES at rung r) = 1 if cleared_r else share of simulations where any remaining game reaches r. As-of the final official score of the last completed game; remaining list with week and kickoff.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.why: Season thresholds settle YES once any game clears the rung, so the realised maximum to date and remaining games define the live state.

nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.label: Player-game probability of a 200/225/250+ single-game rushing total
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.mechanism: Per player-game probability that rushing yards reach a high rung (200, 225, 250) from the compound of carry count and heavy-tailed per-carry yards, conditioned on script and opponent.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.rationale: Mean-based projections put no back near 225 yards; the event, which recurs across seasons (record 296 yards), comes from a lead back getting 30 carries in a lopsided win against a poor run defence and breaking two long runs. The compound distribution, not the mean, decides, and quarterbacks with designed runs are a second, smaller contributor.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.measurement: For each rusher-game: carries ~ NB with mean = player carry share (last 8 games, half-life 4, shrink to depth-slot prior with k=3 games) x team rush attempts, where team attempts are a function of own-model expected margin (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, no betting spread) fitted on 2015-2025 team-games; per-carry yards drawn from the discrete tail of nfl.rush_yardage_tail with the opponent explosive-allowed adjustment; in simulated paths where the team leads by 28+ in Q4 cap the rusher's remaining carries at 2. Report P(yards >= 200/225/250). Calibrate by comparing simulated count of 200+ games per season with the 2000-2025 empirical frequency per season (scale intercept only). As-of start of week.
raw_data: team rush attempts, own-model expected margin
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.why: The 225+ rushing-yard contract is a recurring-tail event needing a per player-game exceedance probability that combines carry volume and the per-carry tail.

nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.label: Leader's scoring behaviour after the game is decided
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.mechanism: Points the leading team keeps adding once the lead exceeds about 35 points, set by the head coach's run-it-up versus kneel tendency, backup quarterback play-calling and whether the trailing team concedes effort.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.rationale: A 52-point margin almost never arises from starters alone; it needs fourth-quarter scoring with backups. Coaches differ: some keep throwing and go for it on fourth down, others run the clock. The existing starter-pull input caps starters but says nothing about points scored after the pull.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.measurement: From 2000-2025 pbp, select game states with lead >= 28 in the third or fourth quarter; per head coach, compute points per remaining drive and pass rate versus league expectation for that state; shrink to league mean with 15 drives prior weight; output expected additional points and their distribution per remaining minute. As-of start of week with current coach.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.why: A 52-point margin needs the leading team to keep scoring after the game is decided; coach and backup-QB behaviour set that.

nfl.weekly_slate_composition.label: Weekly slate size, byes and game windows
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.mechanism: Which teams and games are in the week's slate: byes remove teams, Week 18 includes all 32, and international or Thursday games are part of the same week, setting N for the argmax.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.rationale: With no information the argmax share is about 1/N, and N ranges from about 13 to 16 games and 26 to 32 teams; bye-heavy weeks lift every remaining team's share. A team on bye has zero probability, which the market text does not say explicitly.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.measurement: From the official schedule as of the week's first kickoff: list of games, teams on bye, kickoff windows, roof status; N_games, N_teams; flag postponed or relocated games and their week assignment. Recompute after any schedule change; units counts.
raw_data: schedules.game_id, week, gameday, home_team, away_team, roof
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.why: Number of games and teams on the weekly slate (byes, Week 18 full slate) sets the baseline argmax share.

nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.label: Probability and size of ties at the weekly maximum
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.mechanism: Probability that two or more games (or teams) share the highest total (or team score) in a week, and the expected payout under the $1/N rounded-down rule.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.rationale: Team scores cluster on key values (17, 20, 24, 27, 31, 34) so ties at the top among 26-32 teams are common enough to change expected value; game-total ties at the maximum are rarer but not negligible. The dead-heat rule makes a tied favourite worth well below 1.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.measurement: Empirical 2002-2025: share of weeks with a tied maximum team score and tied maximum game total, by number of teams playing; model: simulate integer team-score PMFs per team-game (from nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean, the catalog key-number PMF input), compute P(tie at max) and expected payout floor(100/N)/100 per named team; calibrate simulated tie rates to the empirical share. As-of week start.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.why: Integer scores tie at the weekly maximum often enough that the 1/N dead-heat payout changes expected value.

nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.label: Era-adjusted historical distribution of season maxima (margin, total, rushing yards)
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.mechanism: Per-season maxima of game margin, game total and single-game rushing yards over past regular seasons, adjusted for the scoring environment and number of games.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.rationale: Rungs differ in rarity: the 109.5 total lies beyond the post-merger record (about 106), the 51.5 margin has been exceeded at least five times since the merger (59, 54, 59, 55 and 58 points in 1976, 1989, 2009, 2011 and 2012), roughly once a decade, and 225+ rushing yards recurs across seasons. Base rates are therefore set separately per rung: seasons with any margin above 45, any total above 90 and any 200-yard rusher calibrate per-game tail fits and guard against overconfident extrapolation.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.measurement: For 1978-2025 seasons compute max margin, max total and max single-game rushing yards; scale for games per season (16 to 17) and league scoring per game relative to the season mean; fit GEV per statistic with a scoring-environment covariate; report P(season max > rung) for the 2026 environment with bootstrap intervals. Report per-rung empirical frequency (seasons with exceedance / seasons) beside the GEV estimate; for the 225 rung use count of 225+ games per season, not a record-break model.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference season and game finder (free, scrape)
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.why: Historical season maxima of margin, total and single-game rushing yards by era anchor the tail and the rung choice.

nfl.week_running_state_by_window.label: Within-week realised scores by kickoff window and market close time
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.mechanism: For the weekly argmax contracts, the highest game total and highest team score already realised after the Thursday, international, early Sunday and late Sunday windows condition what the remaining games must exceed, and the market close time relative to each window decides how much of that is already known.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.rationale: Unlike season thresholds, a weekly argmax is partly settled before the last kickoff: after the early window a 55-point game or a 45-point team score sets a running bar that the late games and Monday night rarely beat, so the named game's or team's probability collapses or rises discretely as windows finish. Ignoring the running maximum treats a live market as if it were pre-week.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.measurement: At each timestamp t in the week: running max game total M_g(t) and running max team score M_t(t) over completed games (final scores, OT included), the list of games not yet started with kickoff times, and for each remaining game P(total > M_g(t)) and P(team score >= M_t(t)) from the integer score PMFs (nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean), with ties at the bar counted as dead heats. The named game or team's probability is the conditional argmax probability given the running bar. As-of the last completed final score; capture the market close timestamp so that positions are only evaluated before it. Units points and games.
raw_data: schedules.game_id, week, gameday, gametime, home_score, away_score
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.why: Weekly highest-scoring game and team markets are partly settled by earlier windows, so the realised in-week maximum and the close time relative to the Monday game are needed state.

nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.label: Season-long any-player single-game extreme by stat (passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, INTs)
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.mechanism: Each non-rushing KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rung pays if any player in any regular-season game reaches it, so its probability is one minus the product over the season's player-games of the chance of staying below the rung, built from each stat's own opportunity-times-yield process: passing yards and passing TDs from dropbacks and efficiency in shootouts; receiving yards and receptions from target share in high-volume passing games; non-passing TDs from goal-line usage; sacks from pass-rush wins against a trailing offence; tackles from defensive snaps and opponent run volume; interceptions from a defender's targets against turnover-prone passers.
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.rationale: The live rung list goes far beyond rushing: 475/500/525 passing yards, 6 passing TDs, 250/275/300 receiving yards, 15/17/20 receptions, 4+ non-passing TDs, 4/5/6 sacks, 20+ tackles, 2/3 defensive interceptions, 2+ D/ST TDs and 100 rushing plus 100 receiving yards. Each sits in a different tail with different drivers, and several were already settled YES early in the season (2 and 3 interceptions, 15 and 17 receptions), so banked state matters as much as the per-game tail. Tackle counts depend on the official scorer's solo-plus-assist tally, which varies by stadium crew.
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.measurement: For each stat k in {pass yds, pass TD, rec yds, receptions, non-passing TD, sacks, tackles (solo+assisted), def INT, D/ST TD, rush>=100 and rec>=100 jointly}: per player-game, simulate the stat from the player's opportunity share (last 8 games, half-life 4, shrunk to depth-slot prior k=3 games) times team volume conditioned on own-model margin and total draws (nfl.model_team_points_mean, never betting lines), with stat-specific yield distributions fitted on 2010-2025 player-games (negative binomial for counts, discretised gamma mixture for yards; tackle counts with a home-scorer random effect shrunk k=16 games). P(rung reached in game) per player-game; season probability = 1 - prod over remaining player-games (1 - p) with a shared-rating-error adjustment, conditioned on the realised season maximum to date (settled rungs = 1). Calibrate each stat's intercept to the 2010-2025 count of games per season above the rung. As-of start of each week.
free_sources: nflverse player_stats (passing, receiving, rushing, defensive: def_tackles_solo, def_tackle_assists, def_sacks, def_interceptions)
raw_data: player-game stats by stat type with game_id and week
team-game plays, dropbacks and rush attempts
home team and official stat crew identifier where available
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.why: Covers every non-rushing KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rung (passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, INTs, D/ST TDs, 100/100 combo), which previously had no inputs in this record.

nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.label: Any-player single-quarter stat extreme (250 passing, 150 rushing, 150 receiving yards; overtime excluded)
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.mechanism: Quarter rungs pay if any player records the stat within one regulation quarter; a 15-minute window concentrates the outcome on explosive plays and on quarters with many possessions (two-minute drills, trailing scripts), so the per-quarter distribution is far more tail-heavy relative to its mean than the full-game total.
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.rationale: The KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rules state that quarter-specific markets count only stats in an individual quarter, not overtime, so full-game projections cannot be scaled by one quarter: second and fourth quarters carry end-of-half possessions, and a single 80-yard play is a large share of a 150-yard quarter.
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.measurement: From nflverse pbp 2010-2025, aggregate each player's passing, rushing and receiving yards by game and quarter (qtr 1-4 only; qtr 5 excluded). Per player-quarter model: yards = sum over the player's plays in the quarter of per-play yards drawn from the player's play-yard distribution (shrunk to position, k=150 plays), with play count negative binomial by quarter index and simulated score state. Season probability = 1 - prod over remaining player-quarters (1 - p), conditioned on settled rungs. Calibrate to the empirical per-season count of player-quarters above each rung. As-of start of each week.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, qtr, passer_player_id, rusher_player_id, receiver_player_id, yards_gained, play_type, score_differential
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.why: KXNFLGAMESPECIALS lists quarter rungs (QPY250, QRY150, QREY150) whose window and overtime exclusion differ from the full-game rungs.

nfl.deep_tail_margin_model.reason: Its GPD tail above 21 points with mismatch and backup-QB covariates and its season-max product rule are exactly the per-game factor for the 51.5-point rung.

nfl.total_distribution_tail.reason: Supplies the per-game upper tail of combined points conditioned on a market-free expected total; must be extended to include the overtime mass for HIGHSCORE.

nfl.slate_total_extremes.reason: Already simulates the weekly argmax of game totals with weather correlation and 1/N splitting; it does not cover team-score argmax or season maxima, hence the companion inputs.

nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.reason: Separate offence and defence rates are needed for the highest-scoring team, since a team can top the week through a weak opponent defence.

nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.reason: Provides the latent strength gaps for pairing mismatches without inheriting betting lines; it feeds the tail models rather than settling anything directly.

nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.reason: Without a shared per-team error, independent per-game tails overstate how many separate games can hit a season rung and understate clustering on one bad team.

nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.reason: Most historic 45+ point margins involve a backup or rookie quarterback on the losing side, so the scenario tree is a key mismatch amplifier.

nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.reason: The joint upper tail of both teams' scores, not each marginal, determines totals above 100; the covariance sign at high totals is the subtle part.

nfl.ot_total_increment.reason: Catalog measurement estimates P(OT) by closing spread bucket and total bucket, a market-derived feature; overtime mass for HIGHSCORE is taken from nfl.ot_model (tie mass from the market-free margin distribution, OT points by rule era) instead.

nfl.weather_total_response.reason: Weather spread across the slate shifts the weekly argmax toward domes; for season totals, record games concentrate in domes and calm conditions.

nfl.non_offensive_scoring_rate.reason: Pick-sixes and return touchdowns are disproportionately present in runaway margins and add points without consuming offensive drives.

nfl.carry_count_forecast.reason: Catalog measurement conditions team rush attempts on the closing spread bucket, a market-derived feature; carry volume for the 225-yard rung comes from nfl.carries (share times lead-conditioned attempts) with the margin from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.reason: Per-carry explosive probabilities (20+, 40+) by rusher drive the conversion of volume into 225 yards; feeds the new player-game extreme rate.

nfl.late_lead_clock_carry_yield.reason: Adds late carries in winning scripts, raising the volume tail for lead backs, but its effect is folded into the script-conditioned carry forecast.

nfl.run_defense.reason: Weak fronts that allow explosive runs are the opponents in nearly all 200-yard games; used as an opponent adjustment to the per-carry tail.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.reason: Caps the starter's further contribution, which limits both margin growth and star-back yardage; the scoring after the pull is a separate new input.

nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability.reason: Week 17-18 resting creates lopsided pairings and depresses resting teams' scores in weekly argmax markets; confined to the final weeks.

nfl.kickoff_rule_regime.reason: The current kickoff rules shift starting field position and points per game, so historical base rates must be adjusted to this regime.

m.rules_text.reason: Strict over-rung versus inclusive 225, OT inclusion, regular-season scope and the 1/N rounding-down rule all come from the text and change value.

m.stat_correction_risk.reason: Only the rushing-yard contract is exposed: a post-game yardage correction can move a near-225 game across the rung; scores are rarely corrected.

nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.reason: Market-free integer team-score PMF with key-number atoms; the weekly team and game argmax and the tie mass need the distribution, not just the means in nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.

m.lifecycle.reason: Used only for market close time relative to kickoff windows of the week, which is timing metadata; no price or line is used as an input.

nfl.ot_model.reason: Market-free source of the overtime increment: tie mass from the model margin distribution and OT scoring by rule era; small but sits in the far tail of the 109.5 total rung.

nfl.carries.reason: Market-free carry-share and lead-conditioned attempts input replacing the spread-conditioned carry forecast; the upper tail of carries in winning scripts, not the mean, matters for 225 yards.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback on the weak side and rested starters on the weak side are the same kind of rating loss and do not stack linearly: once the weak team already starts a backup, resting further starters adds less than it would for a healthy-QB team. The tail growth in expected margin is the separate GPD convexity already recorded as a nonlinearity, so this interaction is only the sub-additive stacking of availability shocks.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit margin exceedance above 35 points on a single combined weak-side availability index versus separate backup-QB and rested-starter indicators; test whether the product term is negative and whether it survives after the GPD convexity term.

interactions.mechanism: Below a lead of about 28-35 points margin growth follows normal play; above it the process switches to a regime where the leader's coach policy and backup quarterback determine further points, so two games with equal mismatch can end 45 or 60 points apart.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition fourth-quarter scoring on lead >= 28 and compare coach-level points per drive; test whether coach identity adds explanatory power for final margin beyond the third-quarter margin.

interactions.mechanism: A 225-yard game requires both upper-tail volume (often 28+ carries, usually in a winning script) and at least two runs of 30+ yards; a high-volume grinder without breakaway speed or an explosive back with 15 carries rarely reaches it.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2000-2025 rusher-games, model P(yards >= 200) with carries, per-carry tail and their product; check that the product term dominates.

interactions.mechanism: Totals above 100 need both teams in their upper tail at once; shootouts are more likely to be tied late and go to overtime, so the OT increment is concentrated in exactly the games that approach the rung, raising the tail beyond the regulation fit.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(OT | regulation total >= 80) with P(OT) overall and the residual correlation of team scores in high-total bins.

interactions.mechanism: With more teams playing and several teams projected near the top, a named team's argmax share falls and the probability of a tied maximum rises; in bye-heavy weeks the reverse holds, so the payout is conditional on the slate as well as the team.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised weekly-max shares and tie frequency on N_teams and on the number of teams within 3 projected points of the top.

interactions.mechanism: When several outdoor games face wind or rain, the argmax mass concentrates on dome games and calm venues; in a uniformly mild week the mass spreads by team quality, so weather matters for the argmax mainly through its dispersion across the slate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare dome-game share of weekly highest totals in weeks with high versus low cross-game spread of forecast wind.

interactions.mechanism: Once a rung is reached the market settles and the next rung inherits the realised maximum, so the remaining-season probability of a higher rung depends on how far the current maximum is from it; the 17-reception rung settling YES removes it and leaves 20 as a far-tail event with a much lower hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest per-week remaining-season probabilities for each stat rung on 2010-2025 seasons conditioning on the realised maximum to date versus an unconditioned season product.

nonlinearities.shape: convex exponential-type tail in expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Per-game P(margin > 51.5) rises roughly exponentially in the expected margin of the mismatch, so a handful of extreme pairings carry most of the season probability.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating in games remaining with a jump to 1 on clearance
nonlinearities.why: P(YES) = 1 - prod(1 - p_g) grows concavely in the number of remaining games and jumps to certainty the moment one game clears the rung, so value decays non-linearly through the season.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in carry volume above about 25
nonlinearities.why: Each extra carry beyond about 25 adds another draw from a heavy right tail, so P(225+) accelerates with volume rather than rising linearly.
Baseline argmax share scales like 1/N, so the drop from 32 to 26 teams lifts every team's share by about 23 percent, a non-linear effect for favourites near the top.
A quarter with two extra possessions roughly doubles the chance of 150 yards because the tail needs several explosive plays, so exceedance rises convexly with quarter play volume.

The rules text refers to quarter-specific markets that exclude overtime, and the series may carry passing, receiving or touchdown rungs; this record has inputs only for rushing, so passing volume, QB efficiency, target share and quarter-window distributions are NOT covered for those variants.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: List every KXNFLGAMESPECIALS market with rules text; if non-rushing or quarter-window variants exist, author a separate player-single-game-stat specials archetype.

unresolved.description: The 109.5 total rung lies beyond all post-merger observations and the 51.5 margin rung has been exceeded only about five times in 50 seasons, so the tail shape for margin and total maxima, and its shift under the current kickoff and scoring regime, is weakly identified; the 225-yard rushing rung is recurring and better identified.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Bootstrap tail-shape intervals and out-of-sample checks across eras; sensitivity of P(YES) to the shape.

unresolved.description: The coach-level continuation policy after large leads is estimated from few qualifying drives per coach and may be confounded with backup-quarterback quality.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Hierarchical model separating coach and backup-QB effects, validated on held-out seasons.
